title.narrative: Uchaguzi Bila Balaa: Violence Free Elections in Coastal Kenya

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the action is to foster collaborative and inclusive community-led prevention of election-related conflicts in Coastal Kenya. The action has two interrelated objectives and corresponding outcomes, as follows:

  1. Strengthen inclusive multi-stakeholder identification of and response to election-related violence risks in targeted communities

¿       ER1.1 Increase capacity of civil society and community actors to peacefully identify and mitigate risks of election-related violence

¿       ER1.2 Increase opportunities for community-led identification and prevention of election-related violence

  1. Mitigate the impact of narratives contributing to electoral violence in targeted communities

¿       ER2.1 Increase the capacity of traditional and digital media to monitor and address election related hate speech and misinformation

¿       ER2.2 Communities have increased access to constructive content that highlights pathways to non-violently address elections-related concerns

title.narrative: The intervention minimised negative risks and maximised positive outcomes on peace and security

description.narrative: Obligatory for all crisis response and conflict prevention/peacebuilding/crisispreparedness actions

comment.narrative: 31 of target community members surveyed who have experienced electionrelated issuesconflicts and report them being addressed peacefully 30 Female 32 Male
66 of target community members surveyed have experienced electionrelated issuesconflicts and report them being addressed peacefully 60 Male 73 Female

The project was implemented in the runup to the 2022 elections in Kenya at a time when political tensions were high in the target communities. Historically elections in Kenya and specifically within the counties of Kwale Mombasa Kilifi Lamu Tana River and Garissa were marred by incidences of postelectoral violence. Locations for implementation were selected following a conflict mapping based on secondary data sources like National Cohesion and Integration Commission NCIC reports and Key Informant Interviews KIIs to identify regions within each county that were classified as hotspots of electoral and postelectoral violence. Based on historical patterns of electionrelated conflict communities at risk of electionrelated conflict and violence were identified and targeted for participation in the project successfully identifying youth and women as key actors. It was noted that women and youth are often hired by politicians to cause chaos and disruption during election campaigns and voting as means of showing populace over other candidates. However women and youth had been given very limited opportunities to play peacemaker roles before the project began hence informing targeting for their participation in this project. Moreover juvenile gangs were often more active and growing in number during the electioneering period. This resulted in the incorporation of youth and reformed juvenile gang members into the project as participants. Their participation in the project enabled them to take part in decisionmaking processes demonstrating the projects relevance to addressing electionrelated violence. The project also enlisted the participation of key influential people and representatives of community groups into project activities. These included youth leaders leaders of womens groups community council of elders social media influencers the media administrative and religious leaders the police indigenous KAYA communities settlements for indigenous Mijikenda people peace committees representatives from the judiciary political leaders local human rights groups and oversight bodies such as Independent Policing Oversight Authority IPOA National Counter Terrorism Centre NCTC as well as the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission IEBC. These community leaders and governing authorities were identified because they were opinion leaders and decision makers in the respective communities.These stakeholders were trained and involved in multiple project activities at different capacities including as election observers peacemakers mediators conflict monitors and participated in joint strategy sessions and referral consultations. These collaborations led to the establishment of referral mechanisms that were used to report and address community grievances connecting the community and existing infrastructures thus promoting peace and unity.As a result 66 of project participants reported having experienced electionrelated conflict and report them being addressed peacefully a 35 point increase from 31 recorded at baseline and 7 overperformance from the overall indicator target of 59.The project not only contributed to a reduction in incidents of conflict and violence but also increased cohesion and integration among community members. This led to more tolerance among different tribes and clans and provided avenues for crosscultural interaction and collaboration an example being reduced incidents of conflict between the Pokomo and Somali from Tana River and Garissa counties respectively. A violent conflict between the Orma and Munyoyaya communities in Madogo that took place in November 2022 was similarly resolved by mediators trained by the project.Increased collaboration among different stakeholders also led to increased awareness of avenues 73 of project participants are aware to address issues that community members may have with the government.
